5.1.2. ArcheangneisssamplesfromtheVredefortDome
Some ABC samples from the Vredefort Dome show strong
irreversibilityofheatingandcoolingcurvesindicatingthatminer-
alogicalchangestookplaceduringtheheatingexperiments.Many
samplesshowaslightincreaseofsusceptibilityaround120–170◦C
(e.g.,samplesLV4“biotitegranite,Q=2”andLV92“granitegneiss,
Q=11”;Fig.6aandb),whichisatypicallow-temperaturetitano-
magnetite(maghemitization)phenomenon(Ade-Halletal.,1971).
These samples also show a decrease of susceptibility around
320–350◦C,whichmayberelatedtotheinversionofmaghemite.
Intensity of susceptibility of the cooling curve is usually higher
in such samples, indicating that new magnetite formed dur-
ing heating. On the other hand, quite a few ABC samples show
reversible heating and cooling curves indicating that no min-
eralogical changes took place during the treatments (e.g., LV46
“charnockiticgneiss,Q=2.9”;Fig.6c).

acterizedbytwodifferentbehaviorsduringtheexperiment.Twoof

sitionsattemperaturesof100–102Kand122–125K,respectively
(Fig.6aandb).However,themajorityofthesamplesshowsonly
oneVerweytransitioneitheraround110–113K(e.g.,LV46,Fig.6c)
or around 100–102K. Carporzen et al. (2006) noted two Verwey
transitionsinthemajorityoftheirABCsamples.Inthisstudyitwas
thecaseonlyfor2ofthe12studiedABCsamples.

7. Discussion
7.1. HighQvaluesandoriginofmagnetization
ItisobviousthatvaluesofNRMand,hence,Qvaluesformany
samplesofthepre-,syn-andpost-impactlithologiesoftheVre-
defort structure – and as determined for the first time, of the
JohannesburgDome120kmtothenortheastofit–areelevated
